nodes.name: Read Recent from Google Sheets
nodes.notes: Reads every row from 'Document Tracker' — the read side of the store, e.g. for a digest or a downstream sync. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Newest First
nodes.notes: Orders items (newest first) so limits and digests pick the most relevant records.

nodes.name: Trim to Digest Size
nodes.notes: Caps the stream at 15 items to protect downstream quotas.

nodes.name: Summarize Content (AI)
nodes.notes: Map-reduce summarization chain — handles long content without blowing the context window.

nodes.name: Anthropic Chat Model
nodes.notes: Chat model powering the AI step (model: claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929). Swap providers here without rewiring. Credential: Anthropic API key. console.anthropic.com → Settings → API Keys.

nodes.name: Render as HTML
nodes.notes: Converts markdown to HTML for rich rendering in email/CMS.

nodes.name: Post Digest to Discord
nodes.notes: Posts to a Discord channel via an incoming webhook — no bot token needed, the webhook URL on the credential is the only secret. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Discord webhook URL. Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy URL.

nodes.name: Archive Digest in Google Sheets
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Document Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

parameters.content:
# Summarize meeting notes: Google Sheets

**Pattern:** AI Summarize & Route · **Level:** Intermediate · **Trigger:** Webhook

## Overview

Fires when a webhook arrives, and covers ocr-&-extraction work end to end across Google Sheets and Discord.

It moves through 9 working steps, in this order:

1. Receive Inbound Webhook
2. Read Recent from Google Sheets
3. Newest First
4. Trim to Digest Size
5. Summarize Content (AI)
6. Anthropic Chat Model
7. Render as HTML
8. Post Digest to Discord
9. Archive Digest in Google Sheets

## Why it exists

Doing ocr-&-extraction work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Receive Inbound Webhook → Read Recent from Google Sheets → Newest First → Trim to Digest Size → Summarize Content (AI) → Anthropic Chat Model → Render as HTML → Post Digest to Discord → Archive Digest in Google Sheets

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and Discord aligned by hand for ocr & extraction
- Pushing ocr-&-extraction events into Google Sheets and Discord the moment they land, not on the next poll
- Ocr & extraction work where "Read Recent from Google Sheets" is still a manual step before Google Sheets
- Ocr & extraction work that only reaches Google Sheets when a webhook arrives, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and Discord in step for ocr & extraction, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Google Sheets or Discord call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 9 nodes in this ocr-&-extraction build
- The ocr-&-extraction AI step is isolated from Google Sheets, so models swap without touching the other 9 nodes
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 9 nodes for ocr & extraction before wiring Google Sheets
- 9 nodes, each with a doc card explaining what it does for ocr & extraction

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Anthropic API key; Discord webhook URL; Google OAuth2 / service account.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Summarization uses a Chain, not an Agent, because the step is fixed — there's no decision about which tool to call, just 'summarize this text.' Posting to multiple channels runs as parallel branches, not sequential sends, so a slow API on one channel never delays the message that was already ready on another.

## Practice exercises

New to this pattern? Try these in order:

1. Add a third notification channel and watch the Merge node's input count update.
2. Change 'Trim to Digest Size' from 15 to 5 and see how it narrows the summary's scope.
3. Swap the Summarization Chain for a Q&A Chain to answer questions instead of just recapping.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Anthropic API key**
console.anthropic.com → Settings → API Keys.
_Gotcha:_ Requires purchased credit.

**Discord webhook URL**
Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy URL.
_Gotcha:_ Webhook mode needs no bot token. Messages cap at 2000 characters.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Webhook returns 404**
Cause: Calling the test URL when the workflow is published, or vice versa.
Fix: Test URL works only while 'Listen for test event' is armed; the production URL needs the workflow published.

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 When this fails

This starter workflow keeps things simple: no automatic retry or error branch yet. If a node fails, the execution just stops — open n8n's **Executions** tab to see which node and why. Ready to harden it? Turn on **Retry On Fail** (3 tries, 2s backoff) on the Settings tab of each external node, and add an error-output branch to a Slack/email alert — every Production-tier template in this library shows that exact pattern.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Discord: give the bot access to the destination channel only, not the whole guild.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole ocr-&-extraction payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.

The webhook path is unguessable but it is not authentication: add header auth or an IP allow-list before this endpoint is reachable from the internet.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your ocr & extraction process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.
